data.situation:
On Friday, Lin accepted the job. Her first morning began in a temporary office behind the centre. The administration team shared a room with the events department. A board showed names and duties. Across the table, Jo introduced herself as Lin’s counterpart at the other centre: they would do similar work at different sites and compare notes each week. Chair: We need someone to report the front-desk questions at our next meeting.
Administrator: I will nominate Jo to speak for both sites this month.
Jo: I can do that. Lin and I will draw up a short list together.
Chair: Good. Please make a reference to the opening hours as well. Several visitors asked about them. Meeting notes
Jo will collect questions from both desks. Lin will check that the list includes a reference to the opening hours. The administration team will send the completed list to the chair before the meeting.

A board showed names and duties. Across the table, Jo introduced herself as Lin’s counterpart at the other centre: they would do similar work at different sites and compare notes each week.
readingBlocks.zh: 周五，林接受了工作。第一天早上从中心后面的临时办公室开始。行政团队和活动部门共用一间房。板上标着姓名与职责。桌子对面的乔介绍说，她在另一处中心做与林对应的工作：两人将在不同地点做类似事情，每周交流记录。

readingBlocks.en:
Chair: We need someone to report the front-desk questions at our next meeting.
Administrator: I will nominate Jo to speak for both sites this month.
Jo: I can do that. Lin and I will draw up a short list together.
Chair: Good. Please make a reference to the opening hours as well. Several visitors asked about them.
readingBlocks.zh:
主席：下次会面需要有人报告前台收到的问题。
管理人员：这个月我指定乔代表两个地点发言。
乔：可以。我和林一起起草一份简短清单。
主席：好，也请提到开放时间，有几位访客问过。

readingBlocks.en:
Meeting notes
Jo will collect questions from both desks. Lin will check that the list includes a reference to the opening hours. The administration team will send the completed list to the chair before the meeting.

会议记录
乔收集两个前台的问题。林核对清单是否提及开放时间。行政团队在会前把完成的清单发给主席。

glossary.zh: 组织事务的管理或行政工作
glossary.note: 本例指管理事务，不是给药这一用法。
glossary.example: The administration team shares the office.

externalEvidence.definition: a method of tending to or managing the affairs of a some group of people (especially the group's business affairs)

glossary.zh: 大型组织内的部门；院系等分支
glossary.note: a department in an organisation；院系也是大型组织的分支。
glossary.example: The events department uses the same room.
glossary.exampleZh: 活动部门使用同一间房。

externalEvidence.definition: a specialized division of a large organization

glossary.zh: 在另一地点或组织承担对应角色的人
glossary.example: Jo is Lin’s counterpart at the other centre.
glossary.exampleZh: 乔在另一处中心做与林对应的工作。

externalEvidence.definition: a person or thing having the same function or characteristics as another

glossary.zh: 主持委员会或会议的人；主席
glossary.note: 可数名词；本例指人，不是座椅。
glossary.example: The chair asks for a report.

externalEvidence.definition: the officer who presides at the meetings of an organization

glossary.zh: 指定某人承担任务或职责
glossary.note: nominate someone to do something；这里为指定任务承担者。
glossary.example: The administrator nominates Jo to speak for both sites.
glossary.exampleZh: 管理人员指定乔代表两个地点发言。

externalEvidence.definition: charge with a function; charge to be

externalEvidence.label: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: Selecting somebody to speak or fulfil a job is a listed use, separate from proposing a candidate.

glossary.note: draw up a list/plan；drew up为过去式。
glossary.example: Lin and Jo will draw up a short list.
glossary.exampleZh: 林和乔会起草一份简短清单。

externalEvidence.definition: make up plans or basic details for

glossary.zh: 说或写时对某事的提及
glossary.note: a reference to something；与推荐信的reference分开。
glossary.example: The notes include a reference to the opening hours.

externalEvidence.definition: a remark that calls attention to something or someone

externalEvidence.label: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: Employer recommendation and mentioning are separate senses; one source form is not one meaning.
